texts.rut.4.12: E seja a tua casa como a casa de Perez (que Tamar pariu a Judah), da semente que o Senhor te der d’esta moça.
texts.rut.4.13: Assim tomou Boaz a Ruth, e ella lhe foi por mulher; e elle entrou a ella, e o Senhor lhe deu conceição, e pariu um filho.
texts.rut.4.14: Então as mulheres disseram a Noemi: Bemdito seja o Senhor, que não deixou hoje de te dar remidor, e seja o seu nome afamado em Israel.
texts.rut.4.15: Elle te será por recreador da alma, e conservará a tua velhice, pois tua nora, que te ama, o pariu, e ella te é melhor do que sete filhos.
texts.rut.4.16: E Noemi tomou o filho, e o poz no seu regaço, e foi sua ama.
texts.rut.4.17: E as visinhas lhe deram um nome, dizendo: A Noemi nasceu um filho. E chamaram o seu nome Obed. Este é o pae de Jessé, pae de David.
texts.rut.4.18: Estas são pois as gerações de Perez: Perez gerou a Esrom,
texts.rut.4.19: E Esrom gerou a Arão, e Arão gerou a Amminadab,
texts.rut.4.20: E Amminadab gerou a Nahasson, e Nahasson gerou a Salmon,
texts.rut.4.21: E Salmon gerou a Boaz, e Boaz gerou a Obed,
texts.rut.4.22: E Obed gerou a Jessé, e Jessé gerou a David.

texts.rut.1.1: Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man of Beth-lehem-judah went to dwell in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
texts.rut.1.2: And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Beth-lehem-judah. And they came into the country of Moab, and continued there.
texts.rut.1.3: And Elimelech Naomi's husband died; and she was left, and her two sons.
texts.rut.1.4: And they took to themselves wives of the women of Moab; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth: and they dwelt there about ten years.
texts.rut.1.5: And Mahlon and Chilion died also both of them; and the woman was left by her two sons and her husband.
texts.rut.1.6: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab: for she had heard in the country of Moab how that the LORD had visited his people in giving them bread.
texts.rut.1.7: Wherefore she went forth from the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
texts.rut.1.8: And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, Go, return each to her mother's house: the LORD deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead, and with me.
texts.rut.1.9: The LORD grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband. Then she kissed them; and they lifted up their voice, and wept.
texts.rut.1.10: And they said to her, surely we will return with thee to thy people.
texts.rut.1.11: And Naomi said, Turn again, my daughters: why will ye go with me? shall I bear more sons, that they may be your husbands?
texts.rut.1.12: Turn again, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, I have hope, if I should have a husband also to-night, and should also bear sons;
texts.rut.1.13: Would ye wait for them till they should be grown? would ye stay for them from having husbands? nay, my daughters; for it grieveth me much for your sakes, that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.
texts.rut.1.14: And they lifted up their voice, and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law; but Ruth cleaved to her.
texts.rut.1.15: And she said, Behold, thy sister-in-law hath gone back to her people, and to her gods: return thou after thy sister-in-law.
texts.rut.1.16: And Ruth said, Entreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:
texts.rut.1.17: Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried: the LORD do so to me, and more also, if aught but death shall part thee and me.
texts.rut.1.18: When she saw that she was steadfastly resolved to go with her, then she left speaking to her.
texts.rut.1.19: So they two went until they came to Beth-lehem. And it came to pass, when they had come to Beth-lehem, that all the city was moved about them, and they said, Is this Naomi?
texts.rut.1.20: And she said to them, Call me not Naomi, call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.
texts.rut.1.21: I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me?
texts.rut.1.22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-law with her, who returned from the country of Moab: and they came to Beth-lehem in the beginning of barley-harvest.
texts.rut.2.1: And Naomi had a kinsman of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech; and his name was Boaz.
texts.rut.2.2: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said to her, Go, my daughter.
texts.rut.2.3: And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her lot was to light on a part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.
texts.rut.2.4: And behold, Boaz came from Beth-lehem, and said to the reapers, The LORD be with you. And they answered him, The LORD bless thee.
texts.rut.2.5: Then said Boaz to his servant that was set over the reapers, Whose damsel is this?
texts.rut.2.6: And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish damsel that came back with Naomi from the country of Moab:
texts.rut.2.7: And she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves: so she came, and hath continued even from the morning until now, that she tarried a little in the house.
texts.rut.2.8: Then said Boaz to Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither go from hence, but abide here fast by my maidens:
texts.rut.2.9: Let thy eyes be on the field that they are reaping, and go thou after them: have I not charged the young men that they shall not touch thee? and when thou art thirsty go to the vessels, and drink of that which the young men have drawn.
texts.rut.2.10: Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said to him, Why have I found grace in thy eyes, that thou shouldst take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?
texts.rut.2.11: And Boaz answered and said to her, It hath fully been shown to me, all that thou hast done to thy mother-in-law since the death of thy husband: and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and hast come to a people which thou knewest not heretofore.
texts.rut.2.12: The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou hast come to trust.
texts.rut.2.13: Then she said, Let me find favor in thy sight, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken kindly to thy handmaid, though I am not like to one of thy handmaidens.
texts.rut.2.14: And Boaz said to her, At meal-time come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she ate, and was satisfied, and left.
texts.rut.2.15: And when she had risen to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and reproach her not:
texts.rut.2.16: And let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not.
texts.rut.2.17: So she gleaned in the field until evening, and beat out that which she had gleaned: and it was about an ephah of barley.
texts.rut.2.18: And she took it, and went into the city: and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought forth, and gave to her what she had reserved after she was satisfied.
texts.rut.2.19: And her mother-in-law said to her, Where hast thou gleaned to-day? and where hast thou labored? blessed be he that took knowledge of thee. And she showed her mother-in-law with whom she had wrought, and said, The man's name with whom I wrought to-day is Boaz.
texts.rut.2.20: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead. And Naomi said to her, The man is near of kin to us, one of our next kinsmen.
texts.rut.2.21: And Ruth the Moabitess said, He said to me also, Thou shalt keep fast by my young men, until they have ended all my harvest.
texts.rut.2.22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, It is good, my daughter, that thou shouldst go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field.
texts.rut.2.23: So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz to glean to the end of barley-harvest and of wheat-harvest; and dwelt with her mother-in-law.
texts.rut.3.1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?
texts.rut.3.2: And now is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to-night in the threshing-floor.
texts.rut.3.3: Wash thyself therefore, and anoint thee, and put thy raiment upon thee, and go down to the floor: but make not thyself known to the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.
texts.rut.3.4: And it shall be when he lieth down, that thou shalt mark the place where he shall lie, and thou shalt go in, and uncover his feet, and lay thee down; and he will tell thee what thou shalt do.
texts.rut.3.5: And she said to her, All that thou sayest to me I will do.
texts.rut.3.6: And she went down to the floor, and did according to all that her mother-in-law bade her.
texts.rut.3.7: And when Boaz had eaten and drank, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn: and she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid herself down.
texts.rut.3.8: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid, and turned himself: and behold, a woman lay at his feet.
texts.rut.3.9: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thy handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thy handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.
texts.rut.3.10: And he said, Blessed be thou of the LORD, my daughter: for thou hast shown more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou didst not follow young men, whether poor or rich.
texts.rut.3.11: And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.
texts.rut.3.12: And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: yet there is a kinsman nearer than I.
texts.rut.3.13: Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform to thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman's part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the LORD liveth: lie down until the morning.
texts.rut.3.14: And she lay at his feet until the morning: and she rose before one could know another. And he said, Let it not be known that a woman came to the floor.
texts.rut.3.15: Also he said, Bring the vail that thou hast upon thee, and hold it. And when she held it, he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her: and she went into the city.
texts.rut.3.16: And when she came to her mother-in-law, she said, Who art thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.
texts.rut.3.17: And she said, These six measures of barley he gave me; for he said to me, Go not empty to thy mother-in-law.
texts.rut.3.18: Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until thou knowest how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest, until he hath finished the thing this day.
texts.rut.4.1: Then Boaz went up to the gate, and sat down there: and behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spoke came by; to whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
texts.rut.4.2: And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here. And they sat down.
texts.rut.4.3: And he said to the kinsman, Naomi, that has come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's:
texts.rut.4.4: And I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy it before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it besides thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.
texts.rut.4.5: Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
texts.rut.4.6: And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar my own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.
texts.rut.4.7: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for confirming all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbor: and this was a testimony in Israel.
texts.rut.4.8: Therefore the kinsman said to Boaz, Buy it for thyself. So he drew off his shoe.
texts.rut.4.9: And Boaz said to the elders, and to all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi.
texts.rut.4.10: Moreover, Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.
texts.rut.4.11: And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders said, We are witnesses. The LORD make the woman that hath come into thy house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel: and do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth-lehem:
texts.rut.4.12: And let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, of the seed which the LORD shall give thee of this young woman.
texts.rut.4.13: So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in to her, the LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son.
texts.rut.4.14: And the women said to Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, who hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel.
texts.rut.4.15: And he shall be to thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thy old age: for thy daughter-in-law, who loveth thee, who is better to thee than seven sons, hath borne him.
texts.rut.4.16: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became its nurse.
texts.rut.4.17: And the women, her neighbors, gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi; and they called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
texts.rut.4.18: Now these are the generations of Pharez: Pharez begat Hezron,
texts.rut.4.19: And Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,
texts.rut.4.20: And Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
texts.rut.4.21: And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
texts.rut.4.22: And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.

texts.rut.1.1: And it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled, that there was a famine in the land. And a certain man went from Bethlehem-Judah, to sojourn in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
texts.rut.1.2: And the name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem-Judah. And they came into the country of Moab, and continued there.
texts.rut.1.3: And Elimelech Naomi's husband died; and she was left, and her two sons.
texts.rut.1.4: And they took them Moabitish wives; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the second Ruth: and they abode there about ten years.
texts.rut.1.5: And Mahlon and Chilion died also, both of them; and the woman was left of her two children and of her husband.
texts.rut.1.6: And she arose, she and her daughters-in-law, and returned from the fields of Moab; for she had heard in the fields of Moab how that Jehovah had visited his people to give them bread.
texts.rut.1.7: Wherefore she went forth out of the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.
texts.rut.1.8: And Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, Go, return each to her mother's house. Jehovah deal kindly with you, as ye have dealt with the dead and with me.
texts.rut.1.9: Jehovah grant you that ye may find rest, each in the house of her husband. And she kissed them; and they lifted up their voice and wept.
texts.rut.1.10: And they said to her, We will certainly return with thee to thy people.
texts.rut.1.11: And Naomi said, Return, my daughters: why will ye go with me? Are there yet sons in my womb, that they could be your husbands?
texts.rut.1.12: Return, my daughters, go; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, I have hope, should I even have a husband to-night, and should I also bear sons,
texts.rut.1.13: would ye wait on that account till they were grown? Would ye stay on that account from having husbands? No, my daughters, for I am in much more bitterness than you; for the hand of Jehovah is gone out against me.
texts.rut.1.14: And they lifted up their voice and wept again. And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clave to her.
texts.rut.1.15: And she said, Behold, thy sister-in-law is gone back to her people and to her gods: return after thy sister-in-law.
texts.rut.1.16: And Ruth said, Do not intreat me to leave thee, to return from [following] after thee; for whither thou goest I will go, and where thou lodgest I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God;
texts.rut.1.17: where thou diest will I die, and there will I be buried. Jehovah do so to me, and more also, if aught but death part me and thee!
texts.rut.1.18: And when she saw that she was stedfastly minded to go with her, she left off speaking to her.
texts.rut.1.19: And they two went until they came to Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they came to Bethlehem, that all the city was moved about them, and the [women] said, Is this Naomi?
texts.rut.1.20: And she said to them, Call me not Naomi -- call me Mara; for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
texts.rut.1.21: I went out full, and Jehovah has brought me home again empty. Why do ye call me Naomi, seeing Jehovah has brought me low, and the Almighty has afflicted me?
texts.rut.1.22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the fields of Moab; and they came to Bethlehem in the beginning of the barley-harvest.
texts.rut.2.1: And Naomi had a relation of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.
texts.rut.2.2: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, Let me, I pray, go to the field and glean among the ears of corn after [him] in whose sight I shall find favour. And she said to her, Go, my daughter.
texts.rut.2.3: And she went; and she came and gleaned in the fields after the reapers; and she chanced to light on an allotment of Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
texts.rut.2.4: And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem; and he said to the reapers, Jehovah be with you! And they said to him, Jehovah bless thee!
texts.rut.2.5: And Boaz said to his servant that was set over the reapers, Whose maiden is this?
texts.rut.2.6: And the servant that was set over the reapers answered and said, It is the Moabitish maiden who came back with Naomi out of the fields of Moab;
texts.rut.2.7: and she said, I pray you, let me glean and gather among the sheaves after the reapers. And she came, and has continued from the morning until now: her sitting in the house has been little as yet.
texts.rut.2.8: And Boaz said to Ruth, Hearest thou not, my daughter? Go not to glean in another field, neither go from here, but keep here with my maidens.
texts.rut.2.9: Let thine eyes be on the field which is being reaped, and go thou after them; have I not charged the young men not to touch thee? And when thou art athirst, go to the vessels and drink of what the young men draw.
texts.rut.2.10: Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said to him, Why have I found favour in thine eyes, that thou shouldest regard me, seeing I am a foreigner?
texts.rut.2.11: And Boaz answered and said to her, It has fully been shewn me, all that thou hast done to thy mother-in-law since the death of thy husband; and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and art come to a people that thou hast not known heretofore.
texts.rut.2.12: Jehovah recompense thy work, and let thy reward be full from Jehovah the God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to take refuge.
texts.rut.2.13: And she said, Let me find favour in thine eyes, my lord; for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken kindly to thy handmaid, though I am not like one of thy handmaidens.
texts.rut.2.14: And Boaz said to her at mealtime, Come hither and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers; and he reached her parched corn, and she ate and was sufficed, and reserved [some].
texts.rut.2.15: And when she rose up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and ye shall not reproach her.
texts.rut.2.16: And ye shall also sometimes draw out for her [some ears] out of the handfuls, and leave them that she may glean, and rebuke her not.
texts.rut.2.17: And she gleaned in the field until even, and beat out what she had gleaned; and it was about an ephah of barley.
texts.rut.2.18: And she took [it] up, and came into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned; and she brought forth and gave to her that which she had reserved after she was sufficed.
texts.rut.2.19: And her mother-in-law said to her, Where hast thou gleaned to-day? and where hast thou wrought? Blessed be he that did regard thee! And she told her mother-in-law with whom she had wrought, and said, The man's name with whom I wrought to-day is Boaz.
texts.rut.2.20: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed be he of Jehovah, who has not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead! And Naomi said to her, The man is near of kin to us, one of those who have the right of our redemption.
texts.rut.2.21: And Ruth the Moabitess said, He said to me also, Thou shalt keep with my young men until they have ended all my harvest.
texts.rut.2.22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, It is good, my daughter, that thou go out with his maidens, that they meet thee not in any other field.
texts.rut.2.23: So she kept with the maidens of Boaz to glean, until the end of the barley-harvest and of the wheat-harvest. And she dwelt with her mother-in-law.
texts.rut.3.1: And Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?
texts.rut.3.2: And now, is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he is winnowing barley in the threshing-floor to-night.
texts.rut.3.3: Wash thyself therefore, and anoint thyself, and put thy raiment upon thee, and go down to the floor; make not thyself known to the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.
texts.rut.3.4: And it shall be, when he lies down, that thou shalt mark the place where he shall have lain down, and thou shalt go in, and uncover his feet, and lay thyself down; and he will shew thee what thou shalt do.
texts.rut.3.5: And she said to her, All that thou sayest will I do.
texts.rut.3.6: And she went down to the floor, and did according to all that her mother-in-law had bidden her.
texts.rut.3.7: And Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was merry, and he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn. Then she went softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid herself down.
texts.rut.3.8: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was startled, and turned himself; and behold, a woman lay at his feet.
texts.rut.3.9: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth, thy handmaid: spread thy skirt over thy handmaid; for thou hast the right of redemption.
texts.rut.3.10: And he said, Blessed be thou of Jehovah, my daughter! Thou hast shewn more kindness at the end than at the first, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.
texts.rut.3.11: And now, my daughter, fear not: all that thou sayest will I do to thee; for all the gate of my people knows that thou art a woman of worth.
texts.rut.3.12: And now, truly I am one that has the right of redemption, yet there is one that has the right of redemption who is nearer than I.
texts.rut.3.13: Stay over to-night, and it shall be in the morning, if he will redeem thee, well -- let him redeem; but if he like not to redeem thee, then will I redeem thee, [as] Jehovah liveth. Lie down until the morning.
texts.rut.3.14: And she lay at his feet until the morning; and she rose up before one could know another. And he said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the threshing-floor.
texts.rut.3.15: And he said, Bring the cloak that thou hast upon thee, and hold it. And she held it, and he measured six [measures] of barley, and laid [it] on her; and he went into the city.
texts.rut.3.16: And she came to her mother-in-law; and she said, Who art thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.
texts.rut.3.17: And she said, These six [measures] of barley gave he me; for he said to me, Go not empty to thy mother-in-law.
texts.rut.3.18: Then she said, Be still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall; for the man will not rest until he have completed the matter this day.
texts.rut.4.1: And Boaz went up to the gate, and sat down there. And behold, he that had the right of redemption, of whom Boaz had spoken, came by. And he said, Thou, such a one, turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside and sat down.
texts.rut.4.2: And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit down here. And they sat down.
texts.rut.4.3: And he said to him that had the right of redemption: Naomi, who is come back out of the country of Moab, sells the allotment that was our brother Elimelech's.
texts.rut.4.4: And I thought I would apprise thee of it and say, Buy [it] in the presence of the inhabitants, and in the presence of the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem [it], redeem; but if thou wilt not redeem, tell me, that I may know; for there is none to redeem besides thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem [it].
texts.rut.4.5: And Boaz said, On the day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy [it] also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
texts.rut.4.6: And he that had the right of redemption said, I cannot redeem [it] for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance. Redeem thou for thyself what I should redeem, for I cannot redeem [it].
texts.rut.4.7: Now this [was the custom] in former time in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to confirm the whole matter: a man drew off his sandal, and gave it to his neighbour, and this was the [mode of] attestation in Israel.
texts.rut.4.8: And he that had the right of redemption said to Boaz, Buy for thyself; and he drew off his sandal.
texts.rut.4.9: And Boaz said to the elders and all the people, Ye are witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelech's, and all that was Chilion's and Mahlon's, of the hand of Naomi;
texts.rut.4.10: moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.
texts.rut.4.11: And all the people that were in the gate and the elders said, [We are] witnesses. Jehovah make the woman that cometh into thy house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and acquire power in Ephratah, and make thyself a name in Bethlehem;
texts.rut.4.12: and let thy house become like the house of Pherez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, of the seed which Jehovah shall give thee of this young woman.
texts.rut.4.13: And Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife; and he went in unto her, and Jehovah gave her conception, and she bore a son.
texts.rut.4.14: And the women said to Naomi, Blessed be Jehovah who hath not left thee this day without one that has the right of redemption, and may his name be famous in Israel!
texts.rut.4.15: And he shall be to thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age; for thy daughter-in-law who loves thee, who is better to thee than seven sons, has borne him.
texts.rut.4.16: And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse to it.
texts.rut.4.17: And the women [her] neighbours gave it a name, saying, There is a son born to Naomi. And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
texts.rut.4.18: Now these are the generations of Pherez. Pherez begot Hezron,
texts.rut.4.19: and Hezron begot Ram, and Ram begot Amminadab,
texts.rut.4.20: and Amminadab begot Nahshon, and Nahshon begot Salmon,
texts.rut.4.21: and Salmon begot Boaz, and Boaz begot Obed,
texts.rut.4.22: and Obed begot Jesse, and Jesse begot David.

texts.rut.1.1: And it cometh to pass, in the days of the judging of the judges, that there is a famine in the land, and there goeth a man from Beth-Lehem-Judah to sojourn in the fields of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
texts.rut.1.2: And the name of the man [is] Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Beth-Lehem-Judah; and they come into the fields of Moab, and are there.
texts.rut.1.3: And Elimelech husband of Naomi dieth, and she is left, she and her two sons;
texts.rut.1.4: and they take to them wives, Moabitesses: the name of the one [is] Orpah, and the name of the second Ruth; and they dwell there about ten years.
texts.rut.1.5: And they die also, both of them -- Mahlon and Chilion -- and the woman is left of her two children and of her husband.
texts.rut.1.6: And she riseth, she and her daughters-in-law, and turneth back from the fields of Moab, for she hath heard in the fields of Moab that God hath looked after His people, -- to give to them bread.
texts.rut.1.7: And she goeth out from the place where she hath been, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they go in the way to turn back unto the land of Judah.
texts.rut.1.8: And Naomi saith to her two daughters-in-law, `Go, turn back, each to the house of her mother; Jehovah doth with you kindness as ye have done with the dead, and with me;
texts.rut.1.9: Jehovah doth grant to you, and find ye rest each in the house of her husband;' and she kisseth them, and they lift up their voice and weep.
texts.rut.1.10: And they say to her, `Surely with thee we go back to thy people.'
texts.rut.1.11: And Naomi saith, `Turn back, my daughters; why do ye go with me? are there yet to me sons in my bowels that they have been to you for husbands?
texts.rut.1.12: Turn back, my daughters, go, for I am too aged to be to a husband; though I had said, There is for me hope, also, I have been to-night to a husband, and also I have borne sons:
texts.rut.1.13: for them do ye wait till that they grow up? for them do ye shut yourselves up, not to be to a husband? nay, my daughters, for more bitter to me than to you, for the hand of Jehovah hath gone out against me.'
texts.rut.1.14: And they lift up their voice, and weep again, and Orpah kisseth her mother-in-law, and Ruth hath cleaved to her.
texts.rut.1.15: And she saith, `Lo, thy sister-in-law hath turned back unto her people, and unto her god, turn thou back after thy sister-in-law.'
texts.rut.1.16: And Ruth saith, `Urge me not to leave thee -- to turn back from after thee; for whither thou goest I go, and where thou lodgest I lodge; thy people [is] my people, and thy God my God.
texts.rut.1.17: Where thou diest I die, and there I am buried; thus doth Jehovah to me, and thus doth He add -- for death itself doth part between me and thee.'
texts.rut.1.18: And she seeth that she is strengthening herself to go with her, and she ceaseth to speak unto her;
texts.rut.1.19: and they go both of them till their coming in to Beth-Lehem; and it cometh to pass at their coming in to Beth-Lehem, that all the city is moved at them, and they say, `Is this Naomi?'
texts.rut.1.20: And she saith unto them, `Call me not Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly to me,
texts.rut.1.21: I went out full, and empty hath Jehovah brought me back, why do ye call me Naomi, and Jehovah hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath done evil to me?'
texts.rut.1.22: And Naomi turneth back, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-law with her, who hath turned back from the fields of Moab, and they have come in to Beth-Lehem at the commencement of barley-harvest.
texts.rut.2.1: And Naomi hath an acquaintance of her husband's, a man mighty in wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name [is] Boaz.
texts.rut.2.2: And Ruth the Moabitess saith unto Naomi, `Let me go, I pray thee, into the field, and I gather among the ears of corn after him in whose eyes I find grace;' and she saith to her, `Go, my daughter.'
texts.rut.2.3: And she goeth and cometh and gathereth in a field after the reapers, and her chance happeneth -- the portion of the field is Boaz's who [is] of the family of Elimelech.
texts.rut.2.4: And lo, Boaz hath come from Beth-Lehem, and saith to the reapers, `Jehovah [is] with you;' and they say to him, `Jehovah doth bless thee.'
texts.rut.2.5: And Boaz saith to his young man who is set over the reapers, `Whose [is] this young person?'
texts.rut.2.6: And the young man who is set over the reapers answereth and saith, `A young woman -- Moabitess -- she [is], who came back with Naomi from the fields of Moab,
texts.rut.2.7: and she saith, Let me glean, I pray thee -- and I have gathered among the sheaves after the reapers; and she cometh and remaineth since the morning and till now; she sat in the house a little.
texts.rut.2.8: And Boaz saith unto Ruth, `Hast thou not heard, my daughter? go not to glean in another field, and also, pass not over from this, and thus thou dost cleave to my young women:
texts.rut.2.9: thine eyes [are] on the field which they reap, and thou hast gone after them; have not I charged the young men not to touch thee? when thou art athirst then thou hast gone unto the vessels, and hast drunk from that which the young men draw.'
texts.rut.2.10: And she falleth on her face, and boweth herself to the earth, and saith unto him, `Wherefore have I found grace in thine eyes, to discern me, and I a stranger?'
texts.rut.2.11: And Boaz answereth and saith to her, `It hath thoroughly been declared to me all that thou hast done with thy mother-in-law, after the death of thy husband, and thou dost leave thy father, and thy mother, and the land of thy birth, and dost come in unto a people which thou hast not known heretofore.
texts.rut.2.12: Jehovah doth recompense thy work, and thy reward is complete from Jehovah, God of Israel, under whose wings thou hast come to take refuge.'
texts.rut.2.13: And she saith, `Let me find grace in thine eyes, my lord, because thou hast comforted me, and because thou hast spoken unto the heart of thy maid-servant, and I -- I am not as one of thy maid-servants.'
texts.rut.2.14: And Boaz saith to her, `At meal-time come nigh hither, and thou hast eaten of the bread, and dipped thy morsel in the vinegar.' And she sitteth at the side of the reapers, and he reacheth to her roasted corn, and she eateth, and is satisfied, and leaveth.
texts.rut.2.15: And she riseth to glean, and Boaz chargeth his young men, saying, `Even between the sheaves she doth glean, and ye do not cause her to blush;
texts.rut.2.16: and also ye do surely cast to her of the handfuls -- and have left, and she hath gleaned, and ye do not push against her.'
texts.rut.2.17: And she gleaneth in the field till the evening, and beateth out that which she hath gleaned, and it is about an ephah of barley;
texts.rut.2.18: and she taketh [it] up, and goeth into the city, and her mother-in-law seeth that which she hath gleaned, and she bringeth out and giveth to her that which she left from her satiety.
texts.rut.2.19: And her mother-in-law saith to her, `Where hast thou gleaned to-day? and where hast thou wrought? may he who is discerning thee be blessed.' And she declareth to her mother-in-law with whom she hath wrought, and saith, `The name of the man with whom I have wrought to-day [is] Boaz.'
texts.rut.2.20: And Naomi saith to her daughter-in-law, `Blessed [is] he of Jehovah who hath not forsaken His kindness with the living and with the dead;' and Naomi saith to her, `The man is a relation of ours; he [is] of our redeemers.'
texts.rut.2.21: And Ruth the Moabitess saith, `Also he surely said unto me, Near the young people whom I have thou dost cleave till they have completed the whole of the harvest which I have.'
texts.rut.2.22: And Naomi saith unto Ruth her daughter-in-law, `Good, my daughter, that thou goest out with his young women, and they come not against thee in another field.'
texts.rut.2.23: And she cleaveth to the young women of Boaz to glean, till the completion of the barley-harvest, and of the wheat-harvest, and she dwelleth with her mother-in-law.
texts.rut.3.1: And Naomi her mother-in-law saith to her, `My daughter, do not I seek for thee rest, that it may be well with thee?
texts.rut.3.2: and now, is not Boaz of our acquaintance, with whose young women thou hast been? lo, he is winnowing the threshing-floor of barley to-night,
texts.rut.3.3: and thou hast bathed, and anointed thyself, and put thy garments upon thee, and gone down to the threshing-floor; let not thyself be known to the man till he complete to eat and to drink;
texts.rut.3.4: and it cometh to pass when he lieth down, that thou hast known the place where he lieth down, and hast gone in, and uncovered his feet, and lain down, -- and he doth declare to thee that which thou dost do.'
texts.rut.3.5: And she saith unto her, `All that thou sayest -- I do.'
texts.rut.3.6: And she goeth down [to] the threshing-floor, and doth according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her
texts.rut.3.7: And Boaz eateth and drinketh, and his heart is glad; and he goeth in to lie down at the end of the heap; and she cometh in gently, and uncovereth his feet, and lieth down.
texts.rut.3.8: And it cometh to pass, at the middle of the night, that the man trembleth, and turneth himself, and lo, a woman is lying at his feet.
texts.rut.3.9: And he saith, `Who [art] thou?' and she saith, `I [am] Ruth thy handmaid, and thou hast spread thy skirt over thy handmaid, for thou [art] a redeemer.'
texts.rut.3.10: And he saith, `Blessed [art] thou of Jehovah, my daughter; thou hast dealt more kindly at the latter end than at the beginning -- not to go after the young men, either poor or rich.
texts.rut.3.11: And now, my daughter, fear not, all that thou sayest I do to thee, for all the gate of my people doth know that thou [art] a virtuous woman.
texts.rut.3.12: And now, surely, true, that I [am] a redeemer, but also there is a redeemer nearer than I.
texts.rut.3.13: Lodge to night, and it hath been in the morning, if he doth redeem thee, well: he redeemeth; and if he delight not to redeem thee, then I have redeemed thee -- I; Jehovah liveth! lie down till the morning.'
texts.rut.3.14: And she lieth down at his feet till the morning, and riseth before one doth discern another; and he saith, `Let it not be known that the woman hath come into the floor.'
texts.rut.3.15: And he saith, `Give the covering which [is] on thee, and keep hold on it;' and she keepeth hold on it, and he measureth six [measures] of barley, and layeth [it] on her; and he goeth into the city.
texts.rut.3.16: And she cometh in unto her mother-in-law, and she saith, `Who [art] thou, my daughter?' and she declareth to her all that the man hath done to her.
texts.rut.3.17: And she saith, `These six [measures] of barley he hath given to me, for he said, Thou dost not go in empty unto thy mother-in-law.'
texts.rut.3.18: And she saith, `Sit still, my daughter, till thou dost know how the matter falleth, for the man doth not rest except he hath completed the matter to-day.'
texts.rut.4.1: And Boaz hath gone up to the gate, and sitteth there, and lo, the redeemer is passing by of whom Boaz had spoken, and he saith, `Turn aside, sit down here, such a one, such a one;' and he turneth aside and sitteth down.
texts.rut.4.2: And he taketh ten men of the elders of the city, and saith, `Sit down here;' and they sit down.
texts.rut.4.3: And he saith to the redeemer, `A portion of the field which [is] to our brother, to Elimelech, hath Naomi sold, who hath come back from the fields of Moab;
texts.rut.4.4: and I said, I uncover thine ear, saying, Buy before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people; if thou dost redeem -- redeem, and if none doth redeem -- declare to me, and I know, for there is none save thee to redeem, and I after thee.' And he saith, I redeem [it].'
texts.rut.4.5: And Boaz saith, `In the day of thy buying the field from the hand of Naomi, then from Ruth the Moabitess, wife of the dead, thou hast bought [it], to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance.'
texts.rut.4.6: And the redeemer saith, `I am not able to redeem [it] for myself, lest I destroy mine inheritance; redeem for thyself -- thou -- my right of redemption, for I am not able to redeem.'
texts.rut.4.7: And this [is] formerly in Israel for redemption and for changing, to establish anything: a man hath drawn off his sandal, and given [it] to his neighbour, and this [is] the testimony in Israel.
texts.rut.4.8: And the redeemer saith to Boaz, `Buy [it] for thyself,' and draweth off his sandal.
texts.rut.4.9: And Boaz saith to the elders, and [to] all the people, `Witnesses [are] ye to-day that I have bought all that [is] to Elimelech, and all that [is] to Chilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi;
texts.rut.4.10: and also Ruth the Moabitess, wife of Mahlon, I have bought to myself for a wife, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance; and the name of the dead is not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place; witnesses ye [are] to-day.'
texts.rut.4.11: And all the people who [are] in the gate say -- also the elders -- `Witnesses! Jehovah make the woman who is coming in unto thy house as Rachel and as Leah, both of whom built the house of Israel; and do thou virtuously in Ephrathah, and proclaim the Name in Beth-Lehem;
texts.rut.4.12: and let thy house be as the house of Pharez (whom Tamar bare to Judah), of the seed which Jehovah doth give to thee of this young woman.'
texts.rut.4.13: And Boaz taketh Ruth, and she becometh his wife, and he goeth in unto her, and Jehovah giveth to her conception, and she beareth a son.
texts.rut.4.14: And the women say unto Naomi, `Blessed [is] Jehovah who hath not let a redeemer cease to thee to-day, and his name is proclaimed in Israel,
texts.rut.4.15: and he hath been to thee for a restorer of life, and for a nourisher of thine old age, for thy daughter-in-law who hath loved thee -- who is better to thee than seven sons -- hath borne him.'
texts.rut.4.16: And Naomi taketh the lad, and layeth him in her bosom, and is to him for a nurse;
texts.rut.4.17: and the neighbouring women give to him a name, saying, `There hath been a son born to Naomi,' and they call his name Obed; he [is] father of Jesse, father of David.
texts.rut.4.18: And these are genealogies of Pharez: Pharez begat Hezron,
texts.rut.4.19: and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminidab,
texts.rut.4.20: and Amminidab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
texts.rut.4.21: and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
texts.rut.4.22: and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.

texts.rut.1.1: Y aconteció en los días que gobernaban los jueces, que hubo hambre en la tierra. Y un varón de Belén de Judá fue a peregrinar en los campos de Moab, él y su mujer y dos hijos suyos.
texts.rut.1.2: El nombre de aquel varón era Elimelec, y el de su mujer era Noemí: y los nombres de sus dos hijos eran Majalón, y Quelión: eran Efrateos de Belén de Judá; y llegando a los campos de Moab asentaron allí.
texts.rut.1.3: Y Elimelec el marido de Noemí murió, y quedó ella con sus dos hijos:
texts.rut.1.4: Los cuales tomaron para sí mujeres de Moab, el nombre de la una fue Orpa, y el nombre de la otra fue Rut, y habitaron allí como diez años.
texts.rut.1.5: Y murieron también los dos, Majalón, y Quelión, y la mujer quedó desamparada de sus dos hijos y de su marido.
texts.rut.1.6: Y levantóse con sus nueras, y volvióse de los campos de Moab: porque oyó en el campo de Moab que Jehová había visitado su pueblo para darles pan.
texts.rut.1.7: Salió pues del lugar donde había estado, y con ella sus dos nueras, y comenzaron a caminar para volverse a la tierra de Judá.
texts.rut.1.8: Y Noemí dijo a sus dos nueras: Andád, volvéos cada una a la casa de su madre, Jehová haga con vosotras misericordia, como la habéis hecho con los muertos, y conmigo.
texts.rut.1.9: Déos Jehová que halléis descanso, cada una en casa de su marido: y besólas: y ellas lloraron a alta voz.
texts.rut.1.10: Y dijéronle: Ciertamente nosotras volveremos contigo a tu pueblo.
texts.rut.1.11: Y Noemí respondió: Volvéos hijas mías: ¿para qué habéis de ir conmigo? ¿Tengo yo más hijos en el vientre que puedan ser vuestros maridos?
texts.rut.1.12: Volvéos, hijas mías, e idos, que ya yo soy vieja, para ser para varón. Y aunque dijese: Esperanza tengo, y aunque esta noche fuese con varón, y aun pariese hijos,
texts.rut.1.13: ¿Habíais vosotras de esperarlos hasta que fuesen grandes? ¿habíais vosotras de quedaros sin casar por amor de ellos? No, hijas mías; que mayor amargura tengo yo que vosotras, porque la mano de Jehová ha salido contra mí.
texts.rut.1.14: Mas ellas alzando otra vez su voz, lloraron: y Orpa besó a su suegra, y Rut se quedó con ella.
texts.rut.1.15: Y ella dijo: He aquí, tu cuñada se ha vuelto a su pueblo, y a sus dioses, vuélvete tú tras de ella.
texts.rut.1.16: Y Rut respondió: No me ruegues que te deje, y me aparte de ti; porque donde quiera que tú fueres, iré: y donde quiera que vivieres, viviré. Tu pueblo, mi pueblo: y tu Dios, mi Dios.
texts.rut.1.17: Donde tú murieres moriré yo, y allí seré sepultada: así me haga Jehová, y así me dé, que sola la muerte hará separación entre mí y ti.
texts.rut.1.18: Y viendo ella que estaba tan obstinada para ir con ella, dejó de hablarla.
texts.rut.1.19: Anduvieron pues ellas dos, hasta que llegaron a Belén: y aconteció que entrando ellas en Belén, toda la ciudad se conmovió por ellas, y decían: ¿No es ésta Noemí?
texts.rut.1.20: Y ella les respondía: No me llaméis Noemí, mas llamádme Mara, porque en grande manera me ha amargado el Todopoderoso.
texts.rut.1.21: Yo me fui de aquí llena, mas vacía me ha vuelto Jehová. ¿Por qué, pues, me llamaréis Noemí, pues que Jehová me ha oprimido, y el Todopoderoso me ha afligido?
texts.rut.1.22: Y así volvió Noemí y Rut Moabita su nuera con ella; volvió de los campos de Moab, y llegaron a Belén en el principio de la siega de las cebadas.
texts.rut.2.1: Y tenía Noemí un pariente de su marido, varón poderoso y de hecho, de la familia de Elimelec, el cual se llamaba Booz.
texts.rut.2.2: Y Rut la Moabita dijo a Noemí: Ruégote que me dejes ir al campo, y cogeré espigas en pos de aquel en cuyos ojos hallare gracia. Y ella le respondió: Hija mía, vé.
texts.rut.2.3: Y yendo, llegó, y cogió en el campo en pos de los segadores, y aconteció por acaso, que la suerte del campo era de Booz, el cual era de la parentela de Elimelec.
texts.rut.2.4: Y, he aquí que Booz vino de Belén, y dijo a los segadores: Jehová sea con vosotros. Y ellos respondieron: Jehová te bendiga.
texts.rut.2.5: Y Booz dijo a su criado, el que estaba puesto sobre los segadores: ¿Cúya es esta moza?
texts.rut.2.6: Y el criado, que estaba puesto sobre los segadores, respondió, y dijo: Es la moza de Moab, que volvió con Noemí de los campos de Moab:
texts.rut.2.7: Y dijo: Ruégote que me dejes coger y juntar espigas tras los segadores entre las gavillas: y así entró, y está aquí desde por la mañana hasta ahora: sino un poco que ha estado en casa.
texts.rut.2.8: Entonces Booz dijo a Rut: Oye, hija mía, no vayas a coger a otro campo, ni pases de aquí: y aquí estarás con mis mozas.
texts.rut.2.9: Mira bien al campo que segaren, y síguelas: porque yo he mandado a los mozos que no te toquen. Y si tuvieres sed, vé a los vasos, y bebe del agua que sacaren los mozos.
texts.rut.2.10: Ella entonces inclinando su rostro encorvóse a tierra, y díjole: ¿Por qué he hallado gracia en tus ojos, que tú me conozcas, siendo yo extranjera?
texts.rut.2.11: Y respondiendo Booz, díjole: De cierto me ha sido declarado todo lo que has hecho con tu suegra después de la muerte de tu marido, que dejando a tu padre y a tu madre, y la tierra de tu natural, has venido a pueblo que no conociste antes.
texts.rut.2.12: Jehová galardone tu obra, y tu salario sea lleno por Jehová Dios de Israel, que has venido para cubrirte debajo de sus alas.
texts.rut.2.13: Y ella dijo: Señor mío, halle yo gracia delante de tus ojos, porque me has consolado, y porque has hablado al corazón de tu sierva, no siendo yo ni aun como una de tus criadas.
texts.rut.2.14: Y Booz le dijo: A la hora de comer, allégate aquí, y come del pan, y moja tu bocado en el vinagre. Y ella se asentó junto a los segadores, y él le dio del potaje, y comió hasta que se hartó y le sobró:
texts.rut.2.15: Y levantóse para coger. Y Booz mandó a sus criados, diciendo: Coja también entre las gavillas, y no la avergoncéis.
texts.rut.2.16: Antes echaréis a sabiendas de los manojos, y dejarla heis que coja, y no la reprendáis.
texts.rut.2.17: Y cogió en el campo hasta la tarde, y desgranó lo que había cogido, y fue como un efa de cebada.
texts.rut.2.18: Y tomólo y vínose a la ciudad: y su suegra vio lo que había cogido. Y ella sacó también lo que le había sobrado después de harta, y dióselo.
texts.rut.2.19: Y díjole su suegra: ¿Dónde has cogido hoy? ¿Y dónde has trabajado? Bendito sea el que te ha conocido. Y ella declaró a su suegra lo que le había acontecido con aquel varón, y dijo: el nombre del varón con quien hoy he trabajado, es Booz.
texts.rut.2.20: Y dijo Noemí a su nuera: Sea él bendito de Jehová, que aun no ha dejado su misericordia ni para con los vivos, ni para con los muertos. Y tornóle a decir Noemí: Nuestro pariente es aquel varón, y de nuestros redentores es.
texts.rut.2.21: Y Rut Moabita dijo: Allende de esto me dijo: júntate con mis criados, hasta que hayan acabado toda mi segada.
texts.rut.2.22: Y Noemí respondió a Rut su nuera: Mejor es, hija mía, que salgas con sus criadas, que no que te encuentren en otro campo.
texts.rut.2.23: Y así ella se juntó con las mozas de Booz cogiendo, hasta que la siega de las cebadas y la de los trigos fue acabada; mas con su suegra habitó.
texts.rut.3.1: Y díjole su suegra Noemí: Hija mía, ¿no te tengo de buscar descanso, que te sea bueno?
texts.rut.3.2: ¿No es nuestro pariente Booz, con cuyas mozas tú has estado? He aquí que él avienta esta noche la parva de las cebadas.
texts.rut.3.3: Tú pues lavarte has, y ungirte has, y vestirte has tus vestidos, y vendrás a la era, y no te darás a conocer al varón hasta que él acabe de comer y de beber.
texts.rut.3.4: Y cuando él se acostare, sabe tú el lugar donde él se acostará, y vendrás, y descubrirás los pies, y acostarte has: y él te dirá lo que hayas de hacer.
texts.rut.3.5: Y ella le respondió: Todo lo que tú me mandares, haré.
texts.rut.3.6: Y descendiendo a la era, hizo todo lo que su suegra le había mandado.
texts.rut.3.7: Y como Booz hubo comido y bebido, y su corazón estuvo bueno, entróse a dormir a un canto del montón. Entonces ella vino escondidamente, y descubrió los pies, y acostóse.
texts.rut.3.8: Y aconteció, que a la media noche el varón se estremeció, y atentó, y, he aquí la mujer que estaba acostada a sus pies.
texts.rut.3.9: Entonces él dijo: ¿Quién eres? Y ella respondió: Yo soy Rut tu sierva: extiende el canto de tu capa sobre tu sierva, que redentor eres.
texts.rut.3.10: Y él dijo: Bendita seas tú de Jehová, hija mía, que has hecho mejor tu postrera gracia que la primera: no yendo tras los mancebos, sean pobres, o sean ricos.
texts.rut.3.11: No hayas temor pues ahora, hija mía: yo haré contigo todo lo que tú dijeres, pues que toda la puerta de mi pueblo sabe que eres mujer virtuosa.
texts.rut.3.12: Y ahora aunque es cierto que yo soy el redentor; con todo eso hay otro redentor más cercano que yo.
texts.rut.3.13: Reposa esta noche, y cuando sea de día, si aquel te redimiere, bien, redímate: mas si él no te quisiere redimir, yo te redimiré, vive Jehová. Reposa pues hasta la mañana.
texts.rut.3.14: Y reposó a sus pies hasta la mañana, y levantóse antes que nadie pudiese conocer a otro, y él dijo. No se sepa que la mujer haya venido a la era:
texts.rut.3.15: Y dijo a ella: Llega el lienzo que traes sobre ti, y ten de él. Y teniendo de él, él midió seis medidas de cebada, y púsoselas acuestas, y vínose a la ciudad.
texts.rut.3.16: Y vino a su suegra, la cual le dijo: ¿Qué pues, hija mía? Y ella le declaró todo lo que con aquel varón le había acontecido.
texts.rut.3.17: Y dijo: Estas seis medidas de cebada me dió, diciéndome: Porque no vayas vacía a tu suegra.
texts.rut.3.18: Entonces ella dijo: Reposa, hija mía, hasta que sepas como cae la cosa; porque aquel hombre no reposará hasta que hoy concluya el negocio.
texts.rut.4.1: Y Booz subió a la puerta, y asentóse allí: Y, he aquí, pasaba aquel redentor del cual Booz había hablado. Y díjole: Fulano, o zutano, llégate, y siéntate: y él vino, y sentóse.
texts.rut.4.2: Entonces él tomó diez varones de los ancianos de la ciudad, y dijo: Sentáos aquí. Y ellos se sentaron.
texts.rut.4.3: Y dijo al redentor: Una parte de las tierras que tuvo nuestro hermano Elimelec, vendió Noemí, la que volvió del campo de Moab.
texts.rut.4.4: Y yo dije en mí de hacértelo saber, y decirte que las tomes delante de los que están aquí sentados, y delante de los ancianos de mi pueblo. Si redimieres, redime. Y si no quisieres redimir, decláramelo para que yo lo sepa: porque no hay otro que redima si no tú; y yo después de ti. Y el otro respondió: Yo redimiré.
texts.rut.4.5: Entonces replicó Booz: El mismo día que tomares las tierras de mano de Noemí, tomaste también a Rut Moabita mujer del difunto, para que levantes el nombre del muerto sobre su posesión.
texts.rut.4.6: Y el redentor respondió: No puedo yo redimir a mi provecho; porque echaría a perder mi heredad; redime tú mi redención; porque yo no podré redimir.
texts.rut.4.7: Y había ya de luengo tiempo esta costumbre en Israel en la redención o contrato, que para la confirmación de cualquier negocio el uno quitaba su zapato, y lo daba a su compañero. Y éste era el testimonio en Israel.
texts.rut.4.8: Entonces el pariente dijo a Booz: Tómalo tú. Y diciendo esto descalzó su zapato.
texts.rut.4.9: Y Booz dijo a los ancianos y a todo el pueblo: Vosotros seréis hoy testigos de como tomo todas las cosas que fueron de Elimelec, y todo lo que fue de Quelión, y de Majalón de mano de Noemí;
texts.rut.4.10: Y que también tomo por mi mujer a Rut Moabita, mujer de Majalón, para que yo levante el nombre del difunto sobre su heredad, para que el nombre del muerto no se pierda de entre sus hermanos, y de la puerta de su lugar. Vosotros seréis hoy testigos.
texts.rut.4.11: Y dijeron todos los del pueblo que estaban a la puerta con los ancianos: Qué somos testigos. Jehová haga a la mujer que entra en tu casa, como a Raquel y a Lia, las cuales dos edificaron la casa de Israel: y tú seas ilustre en Efrata, y tengas nombradía en Belén.
texts.rut.4.12: Tu casa sea como la casa de Fares, al cual parió Tamar a Judá, de la simiente que Jehová te diere de aquesta moza.
texts.rut.4.13: Y así Booz tomó a Rut, y ella fue su mujer. El cual como entró a ella, Jehová le dio que concibiese, y pariese un hijo.
texts.rut.4.14: Y las mujeres decían a Noemí: Loado sea Jehová, que hizo que no te faltase redentor hoy, cuyo nombre será nombrado en Israel.
texts.rut.4.15: El cual será restaurador de tu alma, y el que sustentará tu vejez: pues que tu nuera, la cual te ama, le ha parido, que más te vale ésta, que siete hijos.
texts.rut.4.16: Y tomando Noemí el hijo, púsole en su regazo, y fuéle su ama.
texts.rut.4.17: Y las vecinas le pusieron nombre, diciendo: A Noemí ha nacido un hijo: y llamáronle Obed. Éste es padre de Isaí, padre de David:
texts.rut.4.18: Y estas son las generaciones de Fares: Fares engendró a Jesrón;
texts.rut.4.19: Y Jesrón engendró a Ram, y Ram engendró a Aminadab;
texts.rut.4.20: Y Aminadab engendró a Naasón, y Naasón engendró a Salmón;
texts.rut.4.21: Y Salmón engendró a Booz, y Booz engendró a Obed;
texts.rut.4.22: Y Obed engendró a Isaí, e Isaí engendró a David.

texts.rut.1.1: And it came to pass, in the days when the Judges administered justice, that there was a famine in the land,—and so a certain man went his way, out of Bethlehem-judah to sojourn in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
texts.rut.1.2: And, the name of the man, was Elimelech, and, the name of his wife, Naomi, and, the name of his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion—Ephrathites out of Bethlehem-judah,—so they came into the country of Moab, and remained there.
texts.rut.1.3: And Elimelech, husband of Naomi, died,—and she was left, she and her two sons.
texts.rut.1.4: And they took them wives, of the women of Moab, the name of the one, was Orpah, and, the name of the other, Ruth,—and they dwelt there, about ten years.
texts.rut.1.5: And, they also, both, died, Mahlon and Chilion,—so the woman was bereft of her two sons, and of her husband.
texts.rut.1.6: Then she arose, she and her daughters-in-law, and returned out of the country of Moab,—for she had heard, in the country of Moab, how that Yahweh had visited his people, in giving unto them, bread.
texts.rut.1.7: So she went forth out of the dwelling-place where she had remained, and her two daughters-in-law with her,—and they went on the way, to return unto the land of Judah.
texts.rut.1.8: Then said Naomi to her two daughters-in-law: Go return, each one to the house of her mother,—Yahweh deal with you in lovingkindness, as ye have dealt with the dead, and with me.
texts.rut.1.9: Yahweh grant you, that ye may find a place of rest, each one in the house of her husband,—And she kissed them, and they lifted up their voice, and wept.
texts.rut.1.10: And they said to her,—With thee, will we return, unto thy people.
texts.rut.1.11: Then said Naomi—Go back, my daughters! wherefore should ye journey with me? Have I, yet, sons in my womb, that they should become your, husbands?
texts.rut.1.12: Go back, my daughters, go your way, for I am too old to have a husband,—If I should say, I have, hope, if I should, even to-night have a husband, and should, even bear sons,
texts.rut.1.13: would ye, therefore, tarry until they were grown? would ye, therefore, shut yourselves up from having husbands? Nay! my daughters, for it is far more bitter for me than for you, that forth hath gone against me, the hand of Yahweh.
texts.rut.1.14: And they lifted up their voice and wept, yet more. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in- law, but, Ruth, clave unto her.
texts.rut.1.15: And she said—Lo! thy sister-in-law hath gone back, unto her people, and unto her gods,—go thou back, after thy sister-in-law.
texts.rut.1.16: And Ruth said—Do not urge me to leave thee, to go back from following thee,—for, whither thou goest, I will go, and, where thou lodgest, I will lodge, thy people, shall be my people, and, thy God, my God;
texts.rut.1.17: where thou diest, I will die, and, there, will I be buried: So, let Yahweh do to me, and, so, let him add, if, death itself, part me and thee.
texts.rut.1.18: And, when she saw that, bravely determined, was she to go with her, she ceased entreating her.
texts.rut.1.19: So, they two, went their way, until they entered Bethlehem. And it came to pass, when they entered Bethlehem, that all the city was moved concerning them, and the women said—Is this Naomi?
texts.rut.1.20: And she said unto them, Do not call me Naomi [="Sweet"],—call me Mara [="Bitter"], for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me:
texts.rut.1.21: I was full when I departed, but, empty, am I brought back of Yahweh,—wherefore should ye call me Naomi, when, Yahweh, hath given answer against me, and, the Almighty, hath crushed me?
texts.rut.1.22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the country of Moab,—and, they, entered Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.
texts.rut.2.1: Now, Naomi, had an acquaintance of her husband’s, a man of great integrity, of the family of Elimelech,—whose name, was Boaz.
texts.rut.2.2: And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi—Let me go, I pray thee, to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose eyes I may find favour. And she said to her—Go, my daughter.
texts.rut.2.3: So she went her way, and came, and gleaned in the field, after the reapers,—and it happened to her, to light upon the portion of field-land belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
texts.rut.2.4: And lo! Boaz coming from Bethlehem, and he said to the reapers, Yahweh, be with you! and they said to him, Yahweh bless thee!
texts.rut.2.5: Then said Boaz to his young man, that was set over the reapers,—Whose is this maiden?
texts.rut.2.6: And the young man that was set over the reapers answered and said,—The Moabitish maiden, is she who came back with Naomi, out of the country of Moab;
texts.rut.2.7: and she said—Let me glean, I pray thee, and gather among the sheaves, after the reapers; so she came in, and hath continued from that time, all the morning until just now, and hath not rested in the house, for a little.
texts.rut.2.8: And Boaz said unto Ruth—Hearest thou not, my daughter? Do not go to glean in any other field, neither indeed shalt thou pass on, from hence,—but, here, shalt thou keep fast by my maidens:
texts.rut.2.9: thine eyes, be on the field which they shall reap, and go thou after them, Have I not commanded the young men, that they touch thee not? And, when thou art athirst, then go unto the vessels, and drink of what the young men shall draw.
texts.rut.2.10: Then she fell upon her face, and bowed herself to the ground,—and said unto him—Wherefore have I found favour in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take notice of me, seeing that, I, am, a stranger?
texts.rut.2.11: And Boaz answered, and said to her, It hath been, told, me—all that thou hast done unto thy mother-in-law, since the death of thy husband,—and how thou hast left thy father and thy mother, and the land of thy nativity, and come unto a people whom thou knewest not, aforetime.
texts.rut.2.12: Yahweh recompense thy deed,—and let thy reward be full from Yahweh, the God of Israel, unto whom thou hast come to take refuge under his wings.
texts.rut.2.13: And she said—Let me find favour in thine eyes, my lord, for that thou hast comforted me, and for that thou hast spoken unto the heart of thy handmaid,—though, I, be not as, one of thine own handmaidens.
texts.rut.2.14: And Boaz said to her at mealtime—Draw nigh hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. So she sat beside the reapers, and there was reached to her parched corn, and she did eat and was satisfied, and left thereof remaining.
texts.rut.2.15: And, when she rose up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying—Even between the sheaves, let her glean, and reproach her not;
texts.rut.2.16: yea moreover, draw out, for her, from the bundles,—and leave behind that she may glean it, and rebuke her not.
texts.rut.2.17: So she gleaned in the field, until the evening,—and beat out that which she had gleaned, and there was about an ephah of barley.
texts.rut.2.18: And she took it up, and came into the city, and, when her mother-in-law had seen what she had gleaned, she brought forth and gave her what had been left remaining, after that she was satisfied.
texts.rut.2.19: And her mother-in-law said to her—In what place hast thou gleaned, today? and where hast thou wrought? May he that took notice of thee, be blessed! So she told her mother-in-law, with whom she had wrought, and said—The name of the man with whom I wrought today, is Boaz.
texts.rut.2.20: Then said Naomi, to her daughter-in-law—Blessed, be he of Yahweh, who hath not left off his lovingkindness to the living, and to the dead. And Naomi said to her—Near to us, is the man, of our own kinsmen, is he!
texts.rut.2.21: And Ruth the Moabitess said,—Yea for he said unto me—By my young men, shalt thou keep fast, until they have ended all my harvest.
texts.rut.2.22: And Naomi said unto Ruth her daughter-in-law,—Good, is it, my daughter, that thou go forth with his maidens, and that they meet thee not, in any other field.
texts.rut.2.23: So she kept fast by the maidens of Boaz, to glean, until the end of the barley harvest, and the wheat harvest,—and dwelt with her mother-in-law.
texts.rut.3.1: Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her,—My daughter! shall I not seek for thee a place of rest, in which it may be well with thee?
texts.rut.3.2: Now, therefore, is not, Boaz, of our kindred, with whose maidens thou hast been? Lo! he is winnowing the barley threshing-floor, to-night!
texts.rut.3.3: Thou wilt, therefore, bathe thee, and anoint thee, and put thine apparel upon thee, and go down to the threshing-floor,—do not make thyself known to the man, until he have done eating and drinking.
texts.rut.3.4: And it shall be, when he lieth down, that thou shalt mark the place where he doth lie, and shalt go in and turn aside the covering of his feet, and lay thee down,—and, he, will tell thee what thou shalt do.
texts.rut.3.5: And she said unto her,—All that thou sayest, will I do.
texts.rut.3.6: So she went down to the threshing-floor,—and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
texts.rut.3.7: And, when Boaz had eaten, and drunk, and his heart was glad, he went in to lie down at the end of the heap of corn. Then came she in softly, and turned aside the covering of his feet, and laid her down.
texts.rut.3.8: And it came to pass, in the middle of the night, that the man started up, and turned,—and lo! a woman, lying at his feet.
texts.rut.3.9: And he said, Who art, thou? And she said, I, am Ruth, thy handmaid, spread, therefore, thy wing over thy handmaid, for, a kinsman, thou art.
texts.rut.3.10: And he said—Blessed, be thou of Yahweh, my daughter, for thou hast made thy last lovingkindness better than the first,—in not following after young men, whether poor, or rich.
texts.rut.3.11: Now, therefore, my daughter, do not fear, whatsoever thou shalt say, I will do for thee,—for all the gate of my people doth know, that, a virtuous woman, thou art.
texts.rut.3.12: And, now, although it is true that, a kinsman, am I, yet is there a kinsman nearer than I.
texts.rut.3.13: Tarry the night, and it shall be, in the morning, if he will act as kinsman to thee, well, let him so act, but, if he inclineth not to act as kinsman to thee, then will, I, so act to thee—by the life of Yahweh,—Lie still, until the morning.
texts.rut.3.14: So she lay at his feet, until the morning, and rose up before one could know his neighbour. And he said—Do not let it be known that a woman came into the threshing-floor.
texts.rut.3.15: And he said—Bring the cloak that is upon thee, and hold it. So she held it,—and he measured six measures of barley, and laid it upon her, and he went into the city.
texts.rut.3.16: And, when she came unto her mother-in- law, she said—Who art, thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done for her.
texts.rut.3.17: And she said—These six measures of barley, gave he unto me,—for he said, Do not go in empty, unto thy mother-in- law.
texts.rut.3.18: And she said—Abide, my daughter, until that thou get to know, how the matter will fall out,—for the man will not rest, except he have finished the thing to-day.
texts.rut.4.1: Now, Boaz, went up to the gate, and sat him down there, and lo! the kinsman, passing by, of whom Boaz had spoken, so he said—Turn aside! and sit down here, such a one! And he turned aside, and sat down.
texts.rut.4.2: Then fetched he ten men of the elders of the city, and said—Sit ye down here. And they sat down.
texts.rut.4.3: Then said he to the kinsman, The parcel of land that was our brother Elimelech’s, is to be disposed of by Naomi, who hath returned out of the country of Moab;
texts.rut.4.4: and, I, thought, I would unveil thine ear, saying—Take it over in presence of such as are here seated, and in presence of the elders of my people. If thou wilt act as kinsman, act as kinsman, but, if thou wilt not so act, only tell me—that I may know, for there is none who can set thee aside as kinsman, but, I, am after thee. And he said, I, will act as kinsman.
texts.rut.4.5: Then said Boaz, What day thou takest over the land from the hand of Naomi, also, of Ruth the Moabitess, wife of the dead, dost thou take [it], to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
texts.rut.4.6: Then said the kinsman—I cannot act as kinsman for myself, lest I mar my own inheritance,—do, thou, for thyself act as kinsman in my right, for I cannot so redeem.
texts.rut.4.7: Now, this aforetime, [was the way] in Israel, at a redeeming, and at an exchanging, to confirm every word: A man drew off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour,—yea, this, was the way of taking to witness, in Israel.
texts.rut.4.8: So the kinsman said unto Boaz, Take it over for thyself,—and he drew off his shoe.
texts.rut.4.9: Then said Boaz to the elders, and all the people—Witnesses, are ye to-day, that I have taken over all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s, and Mahlon’s,—from the hand of Naomi:
texts.rut.4.10: Moreover, Ruth the Moabitess, wife of Mahlon, have I taken over, to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off—from among his brethren, and from the gate of his dwelling- place,—Witnesses, are ye to-day!
texts.rut.4.11: Then said all the people who were in the gate, and the elders—Witnesses!,—Yahweh grant the woman who is coming into thy house, to be as Rachel, and as Leah, which two of them did build the house of Israel. Do thou bravely, then, in Ephrathah, and proclaim thou a name in Bethlehem,
texts.rut.4.12: And let thy house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bare to Judah,—of the seed which—may Yahweh give thee, of this young woman.
texts.rut.4.13: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife, and he went in unto her,—and Yahweh granted her conception, and she bare a son.
texts.rut.4.14: Then said the women unto Naomi, Blessed, be Yahweh! who hath not let thee fail of a kinsman to-day,—and may his name, be proclaimed, in Israel;
texts.rut.4.15: So shall he become a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age,—for, thy daughter-in-law who loveth thee, hath borne him, even, she, who is better to thee than seven sons.
texts.rut.4.16: So Naomi took the boy, and laid him in her bosom, and she became his nurse.
texts.rut.4.17: And the women, her neighbours, gave him a name, saying, There is born a son to Naomi,—So they called his name Obed, he, was, the father of Jesse, the father of David.
texts.rut.4.18: These, then, are the generations of Perez: Perez, begat, Hezron;
texts.rut.4.19: And, Hezron, begat, Ram, and, Ram, begat, Amminadab;
texts.rut.4.20: And, Amminadab, begat Nahshon, and, Nahshon, begat, Salmon,
texts.rut.4.21: And, Salmon, begat, Boaz, and, Boaz, begat, Obed;
texts.rut.4.22: And, Obed, begat, Jesse, and, Jesse, begat, David.

texts.rut.1.1: En los días en que los jueces juzgaban, hubo hambre en la tierra. Un hombre de Belén de Judá se fue a vivir al país de Moab con su mujer y sus dos hijos.
texts.rut.1.2: El nombre de aquel hombre era Elimelec, y el de su mujer Noemí. Los nombres de sus dos hijos eran Mahlón y Quelión, efrateos de Belén de Judá. Llegaron al país de Moab y vivieron allí.
texts.rut.1.3: Elimelec, el esposo de Noemí, murió, y ella quedó con sus dos hijos.
texts.rut.1.4: Ellos tomaron para sí esposas de las mujeres de Moab. El nombre de una era Orfa, y el de la otra era Rut. Vivieron allí unos diez años.
texts.rut.1.5: Mahlón y Quelión murieron, y la mujer quedó despojada de sus dos hijos y de su marido.
texts.rut.1.6: Entonces se levantó con sus nueras para volver del país de Moab, porque había oído en el país de Moab cómo el Señor había visitado a su pueblo dándole pan.
texts.rut.1.7: Salió del lugar donde estaba, y sus dos nueras con ella. Siguieron el camino para regresar a la tierra de Judá.
texts.rut.1.8: Noemí dijo a sus dos nueras: «Id, volved cada una a la casa de su madre. Que el Señor os trate con bondad, como ha tratado a los muertos y a mí.
texts.rut.1.9: Que Yahvé os conceda que encontréis descanso, cada una en la casa de su marido». Entonces ella las besó, y ellas alzaron la voz y lloraron.
texts.rut.1.10: Le dijeron: «No, pero volveremos contigo a tu pueblo».
texts.rut.1.11: Noemí dijo: “Volved, hijas mías. ¿Por qué queréis ir conmigo? ¿Aún tengo hijos en mi vientre, para que sean vuestros maridos?
texts.rut.1.12: Volved, hijas mías, seguid vuestro camino, porque soy demasiado vieja para tener marido. Si dijera: ‘Tengo esperanza’, si incluso tuviera un marido esta noche, y también diera a luz hijos,
texts.rut.1.13: ¿esperaríais entonces a que crecieran? ¿Os abstendríais entonces de tener maridos? No, hijas mías, porque me duele mucho por vosotras, pues la mano de Yahvé ha salido contra mí”.
texts.rut.1.14: Levantaron la voz y volvieron a llorar; entonces Orfa besó a su suegra, pero Rut se quedó con ella.
texts.rut.1.15: Ella dijo: “Mira, tu cuñada ha vuelto a su pueblo y a su dios. Sigue a tu cuñada”.
texts.rut.1.16: Rut le dijo: “No me insistas en que te deje y en que deje de seguirte, porque adonde tú vayas, iré yo; y donde tú te quedes, me quedaré yo. Tu pueblo será mi pueblo, y tu Dios mi Dios.
texts.rut.1.17: Donde tú mueras, moriré yo, y allí seré enterrada. Que Yahvé haga así conmigo, y más también, si algo más que la muerte nos separa a ti y a mí”.
texts.rut.1.18: Cuando Noemí vio que estaba decidida a ir con ella, dejó de insistirle.
texts.rut.1.19: Así fueron las dos hasta que llegaron a Belén. Cuando llegaron a Belén, toda la ciudad se entusiasmó con ellas, y preguntaron: «¿Esta es Noemí?».
texts.rut.1.20: Ella les dijo: “No me llaméis Noemí. Llamadme Mara, porque el Todopoderoso me ha tratado con mucha amargura.
texts.rut.1.21: Salí llena, y el Señor me ha hecho volver a casa vacía. ¿Por qué me llamáis Noemí, ya que Yahvé ha testificado contra mí, y el Todopoderoso me ha afligido?”.
texts.rut.1.22: Volvió, pues, Noemí, y con ella Rut la moabita, su nuera, que había vuelto del país de Moab. Llegaron a Belén al comienzo de la siega de la cebada.
texts.rut.2.1: Noemí tenía un pariente de su marido, un hombre poderoso y rico, de la familia de Elimelec, que se llamaba Booz.
texts.rut.2.2: Rut, la moabita, dijo a Noemí: «Déjame ir ahora al campo y espigar entre las espigas en pos de aquel a cuya vista encuentre gracia». Le dijo: «Ve, hija mía».
texts.rut.2.3: Ella fue, y vino a espigar en el campo tras los segadores; y por casualidad llegó a la parte del campo que pertenecía a Booz, que era de la familia de Elimelec.
texts.rut.2.4: He aquí que Booz vino de Belén y dijo a los segadores: «Que Yahvé esté con vosotros». Le respondieron: «Que Yahvé te bendiga».
texts.rut.2.5: Entonces Booz dijo a su criado, que estaba al frente de los segadores: «¿De quién es esta joven?».
texts.rut.2.6: El criado que estaba a cargo de los segadores respondió: “Es la joven moabita que regresó con Noemí del país de Moab.
texts.rut.2.7: Ella dijo: ‘Por favor, déjame espigar y recoger después de los segadores entre las gavillas’. Así que vino, y ha continuado desde la mañana hasta ahora, excepto que descansó un poco en la casa”.
texts.rut.2.8: Entonces Booz dijo a Rut: «Escucha, hija mía. No vayas a espigar a otro campo, ni te vayas de aquí, sino quédate aquí cerca de mis doncellas.
texts.rut.2.9: Pon tus ojos en el campo que cosechan, y ve tras ellas. ¿No he ordenado a los jóvenes que no te toquen? Cuando tengas sed, ve a las vasijas y bebe de lo que los jóvenes han sacado».
texts.rut.2.10: Entonces ella se postró en el suelo y le dijo: «¿Por qué he hallado gracia ante tus ojos para que me conozcas, ya que soy extranjera?».
texts.rut.2.11: Booz le respondió: «Me han contado todo lo que has hecho por tu suegra desde la muerte de tu marido, y cómo has dejado a tu padre, a tu madre y la tierra donde naciste, y has llegado a un pueblo que no conocías.
texts.rut.2.12: Que Yahvé te pague tu trabajo y te dé una recompensa completa de parte de Yahvé, el Dios de Israel, bajo cuyas alas has venido a refugiarte».
texts.rut.2.13: Entonces ella dijo: «Halle yo gracia ante tus ojos, señor mío, porque me has consolado y porque has hablado con bondad a tu sierva, aunque no soy como una de tus siervas».
texts.rut.2.14: A la hora de comer, Booz le dijo: «Ven aquí, come un poco de pan y moja tu bocado en el vinagre». Se sentó junto a los segadores, y estos le pasaron grano tostado. Ella comió, quedó satisfecha y dejó un poco.
texts.rut.2.15: Cuando se levantó a espigar, Booz ordenó a sus criados, diciendo: «Dejadla espigar incluso entre las gavillas, y no la reprochéis.
texts.rut.2.16: También sacad algo para ella de los manojos y dejadlo. Dejadla espigar, y no la reprendáis».
texts.rut.2.17: Así que espigó en el campo hasta la noche; y desgranó lo que había espigado, que era como un efa de cebada.
texts.rut.2.18: Lo recogió y se fue a la ciudad. Entonces su suegra vio lo que había espigado, y Rut sacó y le dio lo que le había sobrado.
texts.rut.2.19: Su suegra le dijo: «¿Dónde has espigado hoy? ¿Dónde has trabajado? Bendito sea el que se fijó en ti». Le dijo a su suegra con quién había trabajado: «El nombre del hombre con quien he trabajado hoy es Booz».
texts.rut.2.20: Noemí dijo a su nuera: «Que sea bendecido por Yahvé, que no ha abandonado su bondad con los vivos y con los muertos». Noemí le añadió: «Ese hombre es pariente cercano a nosotros, uno de nuestros parientes redentores».
texts.rut.2.21: Rut la moabita dijo: “Sí, él me dijo: ‘Te quedarás cerca de mis jóvenes hasta que terminen toda mi cosecha’”.
texts.rut.2.22: Noemí dijo a Rut, su nuera: «Es bueno, hija mía, que salgas con sus doncellas y que no te encuentren en ningún otro campo».
texts.rut.2.23: Así que se quedó cerca de las doncellas de Booz, para espigar hasta el final de la cosecha de cebada y de trigo; y vivió con su suegra.
texts.rut.3.1: Noemí, su suegra, le dijo: «Hija mía, ¿no he de buscar tu descanso para que te vaya bien?
texts.rut.3.2: ¿No es Booz nuestro pariente, con cuyas doncellas estabas? He aquí que esta noche estará aventando cebada en la era.
texts.rut.3.3: Por tanto, lávate, perfúmate, vístete y baja a la era; pero no te des a conocer al hombre hasta que haya terminado de comer y beber.
texts.rut.3.4: Cuando se acueste, te fijarás en el lugar donde está acostado. Entonces entrarás, descubrirás sus pies y te acostarás. Entonces él te dirá lo que debes hacer».
